acceptedFindings.title: Missing essential study design elements
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without description of population, setting, outcome, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and predictor origins, the analysis is uninterpretable and unreproducible.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a full study protocol detailing data source, cohort construction, variable definitions, and predictor derivation.

acceptedFindings.title: Undefined predictor 'pred_score'
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without knowing how pred_score was generated (e.g., which model, trained on what data, potential for overfitting), the validity of performance metrics cannot be assessed.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Document the predictor: was it from an existing risk score, a model trained on the same data, or external? Provide derivation details.

acceptedFindings.title: Analysis is explicitly unbound and lacks pre‑registration
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without a pre‑specified analysis plan, all results become exploratory and cannot support confirmatory claims. The binding status ‘unbound’ and result posture ‘exploratory_standard_table’ indicate that no protocol or AnalysisSpec governs this run.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Create a pre‑registered protocol or analysis specification, bind the statistical run to it, and re‑run the analysis before submitting as a final manuscript.

acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript is presented as final while self‑documented as exploratory and unreviewed
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md#/What This Does And Does Not Show
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The paper admits it is not bound to an analysis plan, lacks a reader‑facing report, and has unaddressed advisory issues. Submitting it as a final manuscript is premature and may mislead stakeholders.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Downgrade the manuscript to an exploratory technical note, resolve all flagged issues, and undergo proper protocol‑governed analysis before resubmitting.

acceptedFindings.title: Confidence intervals missing for AUROC and Brier score
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Point estimates without uncertainty measures do not allow assessment of precision; alpha=0.05 was specified but not used.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Compute and report 95% confidence intervals (e.g., DeLong for AUROC, bootstrap for Brier) in the results.

acceptedFindings.title: No calibration assessment for prediction model
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Good discrimination does not guarantee calibration; miscalibration can lead to poor clinical decisions. Brier score alone is not sufficient.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Produce calibration plot (predicted vs observed), report calibration-in-the-large and calibration slope, and consider Hosmer-Lemeshow test.

acceptedFindings.title: Complete-case analysis without missing data documentation
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Missing data can bias results if not missing completely at random. No information on how many records were excluded or the reasons.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the number of cases with missing data, compare complete vs incomplete cases, and consider sensitivity analyses (e.g., multiple imputation).

acceptedFindings.title: Analysis is unbound and lacks pre-specification
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without protocol binding, results are exploratory and cannot be interpreted as confirmatory; the 'prespecified study question' claim is unsupported.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Create an AnalysisSpec (pre-specified analysis plan) and bind the run to it. Re-run or review for consistency.

acceptedFindings.title: Outcome, exposure and covariates are not defined
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Readers cannot reproduce the study or interpret the clinical meaning of the prediction. Only generic names ‘outcome_binary’ and ‘pred_score’ appear, with no operational definitions.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a complete data dictionary with definitions, measurement scales, and derivation rules for every variable used.

acceptedFindings.title: Origin and nature of the prediction model are undisclosed
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The model that generated ‘pred_score’ is not described (e.g., logistic regression, random forest, external risk score). Reproducibility and internal validity cannot be assessed, and overfitting or data leakage cannot be ruled out.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Describe the model class, training data, feature set, hyperparameters, and any internal validation (e.g., cross‑validation) that produced the predicted probabilities.

acceptedFindings.title: No calibration assessment performed
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: For risk prediction, good discrimination (AUROC) does not imply good calibration. Without calibration intercept, slope, or calibration plot, the model may give misleadingly over‑ or under‑confident predictions.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add calibration‑in‑the‑large, calibration slope, a calibration plot, and optionally a decision curve analysis.

acceptedFindings.title: Sample size is small with no justification or event rate reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Prediction model evaluation requires adequate events per candidate predictor. Without the event rate or a sample‑size justification, the study may be severely underpowered or produce unstable estimates.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the outcome prevalence (number of events), discuss event‑per‑variable criteria, or provide a sample size calculation justifying the current N.

acceptedFindings.title: No missing‑data analysis beyond a complete‑case statement
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Complete‑case analysis can bias evaluation if missingness is related to outcome or predictors. The study provides no flow chart, comparison of excluded vs included subjects, or sensitivity analysis.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Describe the initial sample, record‑level exclusions, and compare demographics of included and excluded records. Consider multiple imputation or a missing‑at‑random sensitivity analysis.

acceptedFindings.title: Incomplete reporting of QA warnings
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript mentions 'advisory issues' vaguely; readers cannot assess the severity of the quality checks.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Explicitly state that the run is unbound and exploratory, and list the specific QA warning details.

acceptedFindings.title: Outcome prevalence not reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The Brier score is prevalence-dependent; without knowing event rate, its value (0.1925) is hard to interpret.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the proportion of positive outcomes in the dataset.

reviewAdjudication.nextAction: Route back to protocol with review-response decisions.
